question: frac{{{{(1 + sec θ cos ec θ )}²}{{(sec θ - tan θ )}²}(1 + sin θ )}}{{{{(sin θ + sec θ )}²} + {{(cos θ + cos ec θ )}²}}}, 0° < θ < 90°, is equal to:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Put θ = 45° in the given expression.

Numerator = (1 + √2 × √2)² × (√2 − 1)² × (1 + 1/√2) = 9 × (3 − 2√2) × ((√2 + 1)/√2) = 9(1 − 1/√2).

Denominator = (sin 45° + sec 45°)² + (cos 45° + cosec 45°)² = (1/√2 + √2)² + (1/√2 + √2)² = 4.5 + 4.5 = 9.

Expression = 9(1 − 1/√2) ÷ 9 = 1 − 1/√2, which is equal to 1 − sin 45°.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 − sin θ.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: [(1 + sec θ cosec θ)² (sec θ − tan θ)² (1 + sin θ)] ÷ [(sin θ + sec θ)² + (cos θ + cosec θ)²]

Formula used: sec θ = 1/cos θ, cosec θ = 1/sin θ, sin² θ + cos² θ = 1

⇒ Numerator part 2: (sec θ − tan θ)²(1 + sin θ) = ((1 − sin θ)/cos θ)²(1 + sin θ)

⇒ (1 − sin θ)²(1 + sin θ)/cos² θ = (1 − sin θ)(1 − sin² θ)/cos² θ = 1 − sin θ

⇒ Denominator: (sin θ + 1/cos θ)² + (cos θ + 1/sin θ)² = ((sin θ cos θ + 1)/cos θ)² + ((cos θ sin θ + 1)/sin θ)²

⇒ (sin θ cos θ + 1)² [1/cos² θ + 1/sin² θ] = (sin θ cos θ + 1)² [1/(sin² θ cos² θ)]

⇒ Denominator = ( (sin θ cos θ + 1) / (sin θ cos θ) )² = (1 + sec θ cosec θ)²

⇒ Expression = [(1 + sec θ cosec θ)² × (1 − sin θ)] ÷ (1 + sec θ cosec θ)²

⇒ Expression = 1 − sin θ

**∴ The correct answer is 1 − sin θ.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Identities

Fundamental relations: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, and cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1.

Reciprocal Relations

sec θ = 1/cos θ, cosec θ = 1/sin θ, and tan θ = sin θ/cos θ.

Value Substitution Method

To simplify complex trigonometric identities, substitute a standard angle like 45° or 30° to quickly verify options.</p
